questions.question: Which statement best explains why interaction testing is essential when components are composed into a system?

options.A: It verifies that each component’s internal algorithms are optimal.
options.B: It discovers bugs that appear only when components exchange data through their interfaces.
options.C: It ensures that the source code of each component follows coding standards.
options.D: It measures the performance of individual components in isolation.

questions.explanation:
Interaction testing aims to find component bugs revealed only when components are used together, focusing on interface interactions [Page 49].

---

questions.question: When performing component testing after integrating several units, what primary aspect should be examined?

options.A: The graphical user interface layout of the component.
options.B: The internal data structures used by each unit.
options.C: The component interfaces that provide access to its functions.
options.D: The licensing terms of third‑party libraries.

questions.explanation:
Component testing focuses on testing the interfaces that expose component functions after integration [Page 41].

---

questions.question: In system testing, why is it important to test reusable off‑the‑shelf components together with newly developed ones?

options.A: To confirm that the reusable component’s documentation is up to date.
options.B: To ensure that the combined system behaves correctly and the components interact properly.
options.C: To evaluate the cost savings achieved by reusing the component.
options.D: To measure the memory consumption of the reusable component alone.

questions.explanation:
System testing checks that reusable and new components are compatible and interact correctly when integrated [Page 49].

---

questions.question: What is the main purpose of component testing that creates “composite components” from individual units?

options.A: To assess the overall system performance under load.
options.B: To validate that the composite’s external interfaces function as specified.
options.C: To refactor the source code of each unit for readability.
options.D: To generate user manuals for the composite component.

questions.explanation:
Component testing of composite components targets the interfaces that provide access to the component’s functions [Page 41].

---

questions.question: How does emergent behavior relate to component composition during system testing?

options.A: Emergent behavior is a design flaw that should be eliminated before integration.
options.B: It refers to functionality that becomes apparent only after components are combined, requiring specific tests.
options.C: Emergent behavior is the same as unit‑level bugs found in individual components.
options.D: It describes the static code analysis results of each component.

questions.explanation:
Emergent behavior appears when components are assembled, and such behavior must be tested after integration [Page 49].

---

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the difference between system testing and component testing in the context of component composition?

options.A: System testing only uses black‑box techniques, while component testing uses white‑box techniques.
options.B: System testing evaluates the interaction and data transfer across component interfaces, whereas component testing focuses on individual component interfaces.
options.C: System testing is performed before any components are built, while component testing occurs after deployment.
options.D: System testing measures execution time, while component testing measures code complexity.

questions.explanation:
System testing checks that components interact correctly and transfer data properly, whereas component testing concentrates on each component’s interfaces [Page 49].

---

questions.question: In the context of component composition, what role does a sequence diagram play during testing?

options.A: It defines the database schema for each component.
options.B: It identifies the objects or components involved in an interaction that should be tested.
options.C: It generates automated test scripts for unit testing.
options.D: It outlines the licensing requirements for third‑party components.

questions.explanation:
A sequence diagram can show which objects or components participate in an interaction, guiding integration tests [Page 49].

---

questions.question: Why is it important to test the “right data at the right time” across component interfaces during system testing?

options.A: To guarantee that each component’s internal algorithms are optimized.
options.B: To verify that component interactions satisfy functional requirements and prevent data mismatches.
options.C: To ensure that the source code adheres to naming conventions.
options.D: To calculate the total cost of ownership of the system.

questions.explanation:
System testing checks that components exchange the correct data at appropriate times across their interfaces [Page 49].

---

questions.question: How does component testing differ from unit testing according to the provided context?

options.A: Component testing integrates several units to form a composite, while unit testing examines single methods or classes in isolation.
options.B: Component testing is performed after the system is deployed, whereas unit testing occurs during requirements gathering.
options.C: Component testing uses only manual test cases, while unit testing relies exclusively on automated tools.
options.D: Component testing focuses on performance metrics, while unit testing focuses on UI aesthetics.

questions.explanation:
Unit testing targets individual functions or methods, whereas component testing integrates units to create composite components and tests their interfaces [Page 41, Page 49].

---

questions.question: Which testing activity would best identify misunderstandings between component developers about each other’s components?

options.C: Load testing of the final deployed system.
options.D: Static analysis of source code comments.

questions.explanation: Interaction testing helps uncover misunderstandings between component developers by revealing integration issues [Page 49].
